summary: Kaniksu NF lookout on Roman Nose Peak, Boundary County, ID; built from 1917, tower blown over in 1999; a 2026 trip report shows its ruins.

facts.design: 30-foot pole tower with L-4 cab (1930s); 29-foot treated timber tower with L-4 cab from 1955, later a flat-roof cab
facts.status_note: Blown over in a windstorm on October 31, 1999; a July 2026 trip report says its ruins can be seen in one photo

access.note: On Kaniksu National Forest land; no closure or permit found in the sources read; the 2026 trip report describes climbing from the lakes

visit.trail_note: Summit now more often climbed from the Roman Nose Lakes to the north, per the 2026 trip report

corrections.why: Sources give the tower as 30 feet (1930s) and 29 feet (from 1955); no source supports 80.5 m
A July 2026 trip report says the ruins of the lookout can be seen in one of its photos

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief's 80.5 m matches neither the 30-foot 1930s tower nor the 29-foot 1955 tower; the story uses the 29-foot figure as the last tower height

notes_for_editor: Brief height 80.5 m is wrong (29-30 ft). The 1967 newspaper accounts (quoted by Forest Lookouts) say the Sundance fire destroyed the tower, but staff lists and firelookout.com's late-1970s staffing run past 1967; the story reports both and does not settle it. Current-site information rests on one personal trip report (sonnybou.ca) and a photo caption. The 1930 and 1970 event years are decade starts. Access is marked public because the lakes and summit climb are described; no closure found, so check with the Forest Service before any visit. Forest Lookouts also quotes a 1921 item about a telephone line to the Roman Nose lookout, so the story limits 'earliest' to named lookout people. Brief's status gone is corrected to ruins.
